root.name: French Defense: Hoffmann Gambit
root.moves: 1. e4 e6 2. d4 d5 3. Qe2 e5 4. f4 exf4

overview: White plays 3.Qe2 and 4.f4 hoping to blunt ...e5 and keep the centre, offering the f-pawn after ...exf4. White can regain the pawn with Nf3 and dxe5, but Black can keep it with careful play. The gambit is seldom seen and considered dubious.

white_ideas.idea: Recapture on f4 and open the f-file with Nf3, Bxf4
Use the e-file and the queen on e2

black_ideas.idea: Keep the extra pawn and develop with ...Nf6 and ...Be7

typical_structures.structure: Open centre with e-pawns exchanged and Black ahead a pawn

character.notes: White takes risks and Black is solid with the extra pawn.

character.reason: An early gambit with the queen on e2.

plans.reason: White plays for tempo with the queen on e2.
